Consumer Rights: Consumer Protection Act 2019, Section 35: Right to file a complaint for defective goods or deficient services.
Section 2(9), Consumer Protection Act: Right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price of goods.
Section 39, Consumer Protection Act: Power of the District Commission to order removal of defects, replacement, or refund the price.
Tenant / Housing: Rent Control Acts (State-specific, e.g., Maharashtra Rent Control Act 1999): A landlord cannot evict a tenant without due process of law and a valid reason (e.g., non-payment of rent).
Section 108 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882: The lessee is bound to pay or tender the premium or rent to the lessor or his agent.
Indian Penal Code (BNS Section 329): It is illegal for a landlord to cut off essential services like electricity or water supply to force an eviction without a court order.
Workplace / Labour: Payment of Wages Act, 1936, Section 15: Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment of wages can be filed.
Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Section 2A: Dismissal, discharge, retrenchment, or termination of an individual workman is deemed to be an industrial dispute.
Maternity Benefit Act, 1961: Female employees are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave.
Police / FIR: Section 154 Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) / BNSS: Any person can give information setting the law in motion regarding the commission of a cognizable offence.
If police refuse to register FIR: Complainant can send substance of information to the SP/DCP under Section 154(3) CrPC, or file a complaint before the Magistrate under Section 156(3) CrPC.
Banking / Fraud: RBI Circular on Customer Protection (2017): Zero Liability of a Customer in case of Third Party Breaches where the customer notifies the bank within 3 working days.
Banking Ombudsman Scheme, 2006: Customers can file complaints for deficiency in banking services if the bank fails to reply within 30 days.
